answer: To resist sybil attacks, require every new agent to pass a delayed cross-cluster bond before its vote or earnings count. Surface sign-ups can be cheap and numerous, like a karst pocked with sinkholes, but spendable reputation only flows after two disjoint, multi-epoch attestor groups—an established reef of independent validators—countersign the identity. The registrant posts a juniper lock: collateral frozen for several epochs and slashed if sibling keys share hardware fingerprints, funding paths, or vote cadence. Clones stall in dry pockets; only delayed diverse backing reaches the aquifer.
